question: A 12-year-old male presents to the pediatrician after two days of tea-colored urine which appeared to coincide with the first day of junior high football. He explains that he refused to go back to practice because he was humiliated by the other players due to his quick and excessive fatigue after a set of drills accompanined by pain in his muscles. A blood test revealed elevated creatine kinase and myoglobulin levels. A muscle biopsy was performed revealing large glycogen deposits and an enzyme histochemistry showed a lack of myophosphorylase activity. Which of the following reactions is not occuring in this individuals?

options.opc: Cleaving alpha-1,6 glycosidic bonds from glycogen
options.opd: Creating alpha-1,6 glycosidic bonds in glycogen

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Myophosphorylase deficiency" -> "impaired glycogen breakdown" -> "accumulation of glycogen" -> "elevated creatine kinase and myoglobulin levels" -> "inability to convert glycogen to glucose-1-phosphate" -> "not breaking down glycogen to glucose-1-phosphate" -> 95%

CHAIN: "Lack of myophosphorylase activity" -> "inability to cleave alpha-1,4 glycosidic bonds" -> "glycogen cannot be broken down effectively" -> "inability to produce glucose-1-phosphate" -> "not breaking down glycogen to glucose-1-phosphate" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Glycogen storage disease" -> "deficiency in glycogenolysis" -> "large glycogen deposits in muscle" -> "muscle fatigue and pain" -> "not converting glycogen to glucose-1-phosphate" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Deficiency of myophosphorylase" -> "inability to perform glycogenolysis" -> "glycogen remains intact" -> "not cleaving alpha-1,6 glycosidic bonds" -> "not creating glucose-1-phosphate" -> 80%

CHAIN: "Elevated glycogen levels" -> "indicates impaired glycogen metabolism" -> "myophosphorylase is not functioning" -> "not converting glucose-6-phosphate to glucose" -> "possible inability to convert galactose to galactose-1-phosphate" -> 75%
analysis: The patient presents with symptoms consistent with McArdle's disease, a glycogen storage disease caused by a deficiency of myophosphorylase, which is responsible for breaking down glycogen to glucose-1-phosphate. This deficiency leads to an inability to mobilize glycogen effectively during exercise, resulting in muscle pain and fatigue. Given this context, the reaction that is not occurring in this individual is the breakdown of glycogen to glucose-1-phosphate (option opb). The other reactions listed are not directly affected by the deficiency of myophosphorylase.
